title: Velour Cloudworks — marketplace & GPU partner integration discovery
next_steps: Redwood to share partner integration spec + onboarding checklist and initial SOW template by 2026-12-07
Velour to provide current VPC topology, firewall rules and GPU fleet inventory (counts + types) by 2026-12-10
Schedule technical deep dive for private deployment and benchmarking (SE-led) week of 2026-12-13
action_items: Lara Kim: send partner integration spec, pricing/commercial model options, and partner deck — due 2026-12-07
Mateo Ruiz: draft on-prem packaging checklist, sample helm manifests, and benchmark script examples — due 2026-12-14
Priya Nair: export and share Velour's infra diagram and current QPS/latency SLAs — due 2026-12-10
summary: Introductory discovery between Redwood (AE+SE) and Velour Cloudworks to evaluate a marketplace connector and potential reseller partnership for GPU-enabled inference. Discussed Velour's multi-tenant GPU footprint, regulatory concerns for enterprise customers, integration models (hosted API vs private VPC connector vs on-prem packaged offering), revenue share and commercial models, and an initial technical plan for a proof-of-concept. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send onboarding spec and SOW template; SE deep dive to be scheduled after Velour shares infra diagram and fleet inventory.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-01 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~62m | Attendees: Lara Kim (Redwood AE), Mateo Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Velour, Head of Platform), Jon Park (Velour, Infrastructure Lead), Aisha Mohammed (Velour Partnerships), Speaker 4 (Velour intern)

[00:00] Lara Kim: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, appreciate you making time. i'm lara kim, account exec on the partners team at Redwood. also with me is mateo, our solutions eng. quick round table?
[00:12] Priya Nair: hey all, priya here — head of platform at velour. jon and aisha are on as well. we're excited to learn how redwood could fit into our marketplace strategy.
[00:22] Mateo Ruiz: hi team, mateo — i run partner integrations at redwood, focused on hybrid/private deployments and runtime perf. we'll try to keep this practical.
[00:30] Jon Park: jon, infra lead. we run a mixed fleet of A100s and 80GB H100s across two regions. our highest demand is inference for embeddings and chat in multi-tenant SaaS flows.
[00:44] Aisha Mohammed: and i'm aisha, partnerships — thinking about go-to-market, revenue-share, and marketplace flows.

Topics (auto): integration models, security/compliance, deployment patterns, billing, POC scope, next steps

[02:05] Lara Kim: cool — high level first: what's the use case you want to enable in the marketplace? is it hosting models you manage, or enabling customers to route inference to velour clusters?
[02:18] Priya Nair: mostly the second. customers purchase a managed model from our marketplace and we want to route inference to their tenant running on our gpu pools. however, some enterprise customers will want private VPCs or even their own on-prem nodes. so we need a flexible connector.
[02:38] Mateo Ruiz: ok got it. there are a few patterns we see: 1) Hosted API — easiest, redwood hosts models and you buy capacity; 2) VPC Connector — control plane still with redwood but runtime in velour's VPC (we ship a connector + agent); 3) On-prem package — customer-managed deployment with a minimal control plane handshake. each has different tradeoffs for latency, cost, and data residency.

[04:00] Jon Park: yeah latency is key, especially for chat. We're also worried about cold-starts with large context windows. how do you manage caching and kv — i mean, the kv cache, or K V cash? (laughs)
[04:18] Mateo Ruiz: no worries — we call it KV cache. our runtime supports persistent KV cache pinned to model shards plus prefix caching at the agent level. that reduces repeated fetching on warm starts. we can show benchmark numbers in the follow-up SE deep dive.

[05:10] Speaker 4: quick q — do you support live model upgrades without downtime?
[05:15] Mateo Ruiz: yes — rolling rollouts with canaries, and automatic fallback to a compatible variant if a newer weight fails. small caveat, on on-prem packaging the operator must allow the agent to pull images from our secure registry.

[06:00] Lara Kim: maybe zooming out — aisha, what's the marketplace commercial model you have in mind? do you want a revenue share, listing fee, or usage-based passthrough?
[06:12] Aisha Mohammed: ideally a mix. listing + revenue share for managed offerings, and a referral/commission for customers who choose redwood-hosted variants. open to multi-year contracts for anchor enterprise customers.

[07:00] Priya Nair: security questions — do you have SOC2, can we see audit logs, SSO/SAML integrations, and KMS support for our customers? we handle regulated clients in fintech and need to be strict.
[07:20] Mateo Ruiz: yes to SOC2, we can provide audit log export and SAML SSO for the console. for KMS — we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and can support HSM-backed keys in private deployments. we'll share the security pack doc.

[08:45] Jon Park: network — in the VPC connector model, what's the expected egress pattern? we have strict egress firewall rules and need to avoid unexpected outbound flows.
[08:58] Mateo Ruiz: the connector can be deployed entirely inside your VPC with no outbound egress except to our control-plane endpoints over TLS on port 443, and you can restrict to a set of IPs. for air-gapped, we also offer an on-prem bundle.

[10:30] Lara Kim: great. i'm going to flag two possible POC tracks: 1) Quick perf POC: we run sample workloads against your GPU pool using a small model to validate latency and throughput; 2) Integration POC: end-to-end marketplace flow integrating billing and the connector. which matters more to you?
[10:50] Priya Nair: perf POC first. if numbers look good then integration POC. we want concrete qps / p99 latency numbers.

[12:00] Jon Park: what telemetry do you expose? we need token-level cost attribution per tenant and per-model tracing.
[12:12] Mateo Ruiz: we expose per-request metadata, token counts, latency breakdowns (scheduling, decode, kv), and you can tag requests with tenant_id for billing. logs can be shipped to your SIEM.

[14:00] Aisha Mohammed: commercial question — do you support white-labeling for marketplace listings? some partners want to present the offering under their brand.
[14:10] Lara Kim: yes, we have partner white-label options in the reseller playbook. we'll include the playbook in the follow-up.

[16:05] Priya Nair: on the technical side, what runtime flexibility do we have for quantized models and fp16 vs int8? some of our models are custom quantized and we can't sacrifice quality.
[16:24] Mateo Ruiz: our runtime supports multiple quantization profiles and we can bind models to specific kernel paths. if you're sensitive to accuracy, we can pin a non-quantized variant and we also support mixed-precision options. we'll surface expected token-cost delta in the integration spec.

[18:30] Jon Park: curious: how do you handle multi-tenancy on shared GPUs? isolation concerns — noisy neighbor issues if multiple tenants hit same card.
[18:44] Mateo Ruiz: we provide both logical isolation via scheduling (dedicated streams, CUDA MPS) and absolute isolation via dedicated pools (reserved slices). for multi-tenant marketplace, most partners opt for soft isolation + autoscaling thresholds; for security-conscious customers we recommend dedicated pools.

[21:00] Lara Kim: question on billing: do you prefer usage passthrough where velour bills and pays us, or direct billing with revenue share? this impacts invoicing complexity.
[21:15] Aisha Mohammed: we prefer to own customer invoicing, but open to co-billing for enterprise anchors. need options.

[23:00] Mateo Ruiz: operational note: if you want to own billing, we can emit per-tenant usage records (CDR-like) that you can ingest into your billing system. otherwise we can handle metering and invoice your customers directly and then settle with a partner % share.

[25:12] Priya Nair: regulatory — data residency. we have customers in eu who require data never leaves eu regions. does redwood offer region pinning?
[25:26] Mateo Ruiz: yes — region pinning is supported. our router policies can pin requests to specific regions and we can host control-plane instances in EU if needed (private deployment). we'll add region-residency checklist to the security pack.

[28:30] Speaker 4: small nit: will the connector be container-based or VM?
[28:36] Mateo Ruiz: connector is a containerized agent, we provide helm charts and a minimal daemonset. for bare-metal on-prem we have a systemd installer too.

[30:00] Lara Kim: let's talk POC scope items — mateo, could you sketch the perf POC steps?
[30:10] Mateo Ruiz: sure: 1) exchange SSH keys / service account for limited test access or deploy agent in your staging VPC; 2) run 3 canonical workloads (chat short/long context, embeddings, rerank) with controlled loads; 3) collect p50/p95/p99 and token costs; 4) iterate on batch sizes, kv settings, and kernel profiles; 5) produce a short perf report. expect 2–3 weeks for initial run.

[32:00] Jon Park: sample data — we will anonymize and provide typical prompt sets. what do you need for benchmarking?
[32:10] Mateo Ruiz: prompt corpus, expected concurrency, model variants and token lengths. also a representative dataset for embeddings. we'll give a template.

[34:00] Aisha Mohammed: on timelines — we'd like a pilot ready by end of q1 2027. is that realistic?
[34:10] Lara Kim: yes, q1 pilot is feasible if we start POC this month. we'll align calendar after we get your infra docs.

[36:25] Priya Nair: security doc request again — we need SOC2 report, pen test summary, and the audit log export format.
[36:36] Lara Kim: we'll attach the security pack and SOC2 summary in the follow-up.

[38:00] Jon Park: one more: if we want on-prem packaged option, what are licensing terms and support SLAs?
[38:10] Lara Kim: we offer enterprise private licensing with annual platform fees plus support tier (bronze/silver/gold). on-prem SLA and escalation process vary by tier. we'll include options in the SOW template.

[40:30] Mateo Ruiz: technical caveat — for air-gapped customers we require occasional outbound for certificate rotation; if that is impossible, we do a fully offline install but it adds ops overhead and we need a signed acceptance.

[43:00] Aisha Mohammed: are there references or partners already doing similar marketplace integrations?
[43:10] Lara Kim: yes — we've done similar integrations with a few channel partners and large resellers; we'll share anonymized case studies and a partner playbook.

[45:25] Priya Nair: okay sounds good. any blockers on your side?
[45:32] Lara Kim: none. we'll follow up with the docs and propose dates for the SE deep dive.

[46:00] Transcript noise: (some crosstalk) "uh-huh" "yeah" "mm"

[47:15] Mateo Ruiz: quick notes on metrics we'll collect in POC: token throughput per GPU, p95 latency for 2048 tokens, cold-start variance, memory utilization per model, and cost per 1k tokens under different quantization profiles.

[50:00] Jon Park: curious about scheduling. can we do GPU slicing per tenancy? we want to limit memory interfering across tenants.
[50:12] Mateo Ruiz: yes, we support slicer-based allocation and pinned memory maps. for strict isolation you'd reserve entire GPUs and tie a nodepool to a tenant.

[52:30] Aisha Mohammed: go-to-market question — what co-marketing support do you provide for partners launching offerings?
[52:40] Lara Kim: we offer joint press release templates, co-branded datasheets, a partner launch checklist, and SDR enablement sessions. details in partner playbook.

[55:00] Priya Nair: logistics — who will be our primary Redwood contact?
[55:07] Lara Kim: i'll be primary for commercial & partner ops, mateo will be technical.

[56:20] Lara Kim: recap quick: 1) redwood to send partner integration spec, security pack, partner playbook, and SOW template by 12/07; 2) velour to share infra diagram and fleet inventory by 12/10; 3) schedule SE deep dive week of 12/13; 4) perf POC w/in 2–3 weeks after access. any additions?
[56:45] Priya Nair: that covers it, thanks.

[58:00] Final logistics: shared drive links mentioned — Drive: /velour/redwood/Partner_Onboarding_Deck.pdf; doc: /velour/redwood/POC_Template.xlsx
[59:10] Speaker 4: thank you everyone.
[59:25] Meeting ends ~62:00

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had a few proper noun misreads (e.g., "K V cash" for KV cache), and occasional speaker attribution issues.
